This application coming on for admission this day, the co  following:
 ORDER

This is first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 o f the Cr.P.C. for grant of regular bail relating to FIR No.81/2023 dated 20.6.2023, registered at Police Station - Umraoganj,
District - Raisen for commission of offence under Sections 420, 465,467, 468, 471 and 34 of IPC.

He is in detention since 07.07.2023.
2.

As per the prosecution story, Rohit Narvariya through his Munshi Bilal Khan purchased 50 quintal wheat from Dharmendra Meena worth Rs.1,10,000/- and 115 quintal wheat worth Rs.2,50,000/- from Ramswaroop Meena.

They also purchased wheat from various other farmers,
namely, Toofan Meena, Awadhnarayan Meena, Trilok Meena, Santbabu Meena and issued cheques to them of Aaru Enterprises belonging to Rohit Narvariya.
When aforesaid cheques were presented by the farmers in Bank for encashment, they all stood dishnoured.
As such Rohit Narvariya and Bilal Khan cheated the farmers and did not pay an amount of almost Rs.56,00,000/-

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant has n o t committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated.
It is submitted that applicant is ready to deposit half of the amount cheated by him before the trial Court under protest.
It is further submitted that after investigation charge sheet has already been filed.
The final conclusion of the trial will take considerable time.
Therefore, it is prayed that applicant may be released on bail pending the trial as co- accused Bilal Khan has already been released on bail.
4 . On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the prayer for grant of bail to the applicant.
5. In this case, allegation against the present applicant and co- accused are of cheating of Rs.56,00,000/-.
Applicant himself wanted to deposit Rs.26,50,000/- before the trial Court under protest.
Having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case including the detention period of the applicant, I am inclined to release him on bail.
Consequently, this first bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

6. It is directed that applicant - Rohit Narwariya be released on bail upon his depositing Rs.26,50,000/- (Rupees twenty six lakh fifty thousand only) in form of Fixed Deposit of some Nationalized Bank before the trial Court which shall not be encashable without prior permission of the trial Court and upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
7.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
8 . Disbursement of the amount so deposited by the applicant under protest before the trial Court shall be subject to final decision of the trial Court Certified copy as per rules.
